title: Grateful Dead Live at Music Hall on 1973-12-01
lineage: Maxell UD90's > Nakamichi CR-5A > Edirol FA-66 > Wavelab > R8Brain > CD-Wave > TLH > FLAC 1644 tagged. Transfer by Andrew F.
source: 2 source matrix by dusborne Soundboard (shnid:112205) SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat (44.1k); Transfer Info: Dat (Sony R500) -> Tascam SS-R05 -> Adobe Audition v3.0 -> Samplitude Professional 11.2 -> FLAC and Audience (shnid:110781) FOB AUD Source: Unknown equipment > MAC taped by Bill Degen. This transfer is 1st Gen cassettes, kindly provided by Tim Friend.

ai_review.summary: Brilliant matrix recording captures a high‑energy show with a smoking 'Playing in the Band > Uncle John’s Band' sequence and strong finishes, though a few listeners note occasional sound thinning.
ai_review.review: The Dusborne MTX blend is praised as crystal‑clear and well balanced, delivering an immersive listening experience. Musically the concert shines on the extended 'Playing in the Band' segue into 'Uncle John’s Band' and a powerful finish, while one reviewer mentions a slight drop‑out of detail during 'Row Jimmy'. Overall sentiment leans positive despite a lone critical note.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the show and recording highly (4‑5 stars) highlighting superb performance and excellent matrix sound, offset by one zero‑star comment about occasional thin audio; weighted average yields ~4.3.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Dusborne MTX blend praised as brilliant and very well balanced; clear overall with only minor thinning of sound on certain tracks (e.g., Row Jimmy).

standout_songs: Playing in the Band > Uncle John's Band > Playin' reprise
show_quality.setlist_flow: Second set launches with a tight 'Playin' in the Band' segue into an expansive 'Uncle John's Band', then weaves back to familiar themes before closing strong; audience banter adds to the flow.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar work is highlighted, especially his riff that drives the strong finish of the 'Playing' sequence.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith contributes supportive textures during the final jam, reinforcing Garcia’s lead.
